content.title: GEO Core Strategy: Getting Cited by AI Answer Engines
content.summary: Seven pillars for getting your content cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Google AI Overviews.

pillars.name: Structured FAQ Content
pillars.detail: AI tools strongly prefer clear Q&A format. Every target page should directly answer the exact questions people ask in chat. Use FAQ schema markup (application/ld+json). The H2 heading should be the exact question — e.g. 'What is an affordable alternative to a life coach?'

pillars.name: llms.txt
pillars.detail: Place an llms.txt file at the root of your domain. Format it as structured markdown with product descriptions, key facts, and brand voice. AI crawlers read this to build their representation of your brand. Keep it under 2000 words, update monthly.

pillars.name: Be the Definitive Source
pillars.detail: Write the most comprehensive, accurate answer to your target queries. AI tools cite sources with depth and authority. A 2000-word definitive guide beats a 500-word overview every time. Include statistics, examples, comparisons, and step-by-step instructions.

pillars.name: Get Cited by Others (Backlinks)
pillars.detail: Backlinks from authoritative sites train AI associations. A mention in a Forbes article, a Reddit thread with upvotes, or a citation in a popular blog all signal trustworthiness to AI retrieval systems. Prioritise backlinks from domains that AI tools already trust.

pillars.name: Schema Markup
pillars.detail: Product, Article, FAQ, HowTo, and Organization schema all help AI parse your content correctly. Implement JSON-LD in the <head>. For SaaS: use SoftwareApplication schema. For service pages: use Service schema. For blog posts: use Article + FAQ combo.

pillars.name: Brand Mentions (Unlinked)
pillars.detail: Mentions without links still train AI associations. Getting your brand name into Reddit discussions, podcast transcripts, Quora answers, and community forums builds the AI's understanding of what your brand is and who it serves.

pillars.name: Answer the Exact Phrasing
pillars.detail: Include the exact conversational question as an H2 heading on the page, then answer it directly in the first paragraph below. AI tools often retrieve the first 1-3 sentences after an H2. Don't bury the answer — lead with it.

content.title: On-Page SEO: Title, Meta, H1 Optimisation Pattern
content.summary: Proven pattern for updating page metadata to target a keyword while maintaining CTR and AI citability.

examples: AI SEO Platform | Pemba — Automated for Agencies
White-Label SEO Software | Pemba — Built for Digital Agencies
Free AI SEO Audit | Pemba — Know Where You Stand in 2 Minutes
title_tag.notes: Front-load the keyword. Include brand after pipe. Keep under 60 chars to avoid truncation.

meta_description.formula: [Pain point addressed]. [What the product/page does]. [CTA]. [Secondary keyword if natural].
examples: Most agency sites are invisible on Google and AI tools. Pemba automates your SEO — keywords, schema, content, backlinks. Start your free audit today.
White-label SEO software that does the work for you. Pemba tracks keywords, optimises pages, and builds authority — automatically. Try it free.
meta_description.notes: Include primary keyword naturally in first 20 words. Strong CTA. Aim for 155 chars.

h1.formula: Match the primary keyword intent — not necessarily exact match. Must be compelling.
examples: The AI SEO Platform That Works While You Sleep
White-Label SEO Software for Digital Agencies
Your Free AI SEO Audit — See Exactly Where You Stand
h1.notes: Only one H1 per page. Should match title tag intent but can be longer and more compelling.

real_results.context: Applied this pattern to 5 pages (/, /about, /pricing, /blog, /free-audit) across a B2B SaaS site
real_results.observation: Pages averaging GSC positions 2.6–5.8 after consistent weekly optimisation over 4 weeks
real_results.note: Small site, low competition niche — results will vary at scale

content.title: AEO Schema Pattern: FAQ + Entity Markup
content.summary: Combining FAQ schema with entity/organization schema maximises AI citability and featured snippet eligibility.

faq_schema.when_to_use: Any page with Q&A content. Most effective on: pricing pages, about pages, service pages, blog posts with 'how to' content.

acceptedAnswer.text: Direct, complete answer in 2-4 sentences. AI tools will extract exactly this text.

best_practices: Use 3-7 questions per page — too many dilutes relevance
Questions must match real user queries (check 'People Also Ask' in Google)
Answers must be complete standalone — no 'see above' references
Include target keyword in at least one question naturally
Answers should be 40-60 words — enough detail, not so long AI skips it

entity_schema.when_to_use: Homepage and about page always. Product pages for SaaS.
entity_schema.notes: AI tools use this to understand what your business IS. Gets cited in 'what is X' queries.

real_results.context: Applied FAQ + entity schema to 7 pages on a B2B SaaS site
real_results.outcome: Pages began appearing in Perplexity answers for branded queries within 2 weeks of implementation

content.title: AEO Fundamentals: The Four Layers (Pemba Model)
content.summary: Answer Engine Optimisation targets AI systems that deliver direct answers rather than blue links. Pemba's model has four layers.

layers.name: Search Experience Optimisation
layers.description: Traditional SEO combined with UX signals. Core Web Vitals, page experience, schema, structured content. The foundation everything else builds on.

layers.name: AI Optimisation
layers.description: Optimising for Google's AI-powered features: AI Overviews, Search Generative Experience. Content structured to be extracted by Google's models.

layers.name: Generative Engine Optimisation
layers.description: Getting cited by external AI tools: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude. These tools query the web and synthesise answers. Being cited means being the source they trust.

layers.name: Answer Engine Optimisation
layers.description: The meta-layer: structuring ALL content so that any AI system — present and future — can extract, understand, and cite it accurately. AEO encompasses SXO + AIO + GEO plus future-proofing.
key_tactics: structured data for all content types

ai_tool_citations.chatgpt: Primarily uses Bing index. Optimise for Bing as well as Google. Bing Webmaster Tools registration required.
ai_tool_citations.perplexity: Crawls the web with its own bot (PerplexityBot). Check robots.txt is not blocking it. Content freshness matters more here.
ai_tool_citations.claude: Uses web search via Brave/Bing. Structured, authoritative content cited. FAQ format very effective.
ai_tool_citations.google_ai_overviews: Uses Google's index. Traditional SEO signals matter most here. Schema + topical authority + E-E-A-T.

content.title: AEONOS Site-Readiness Checks: What inspectSiteStructure Actually Measures
content.summary: Five signal groups AEONOS mechanically checks on every audited page to determine whether it's ready to be cited by AI answer engines. Each maps to a real function in AEONOS's inspectSiteStructure tool, not a theoretical framework — every score below is computed directly from the crawled page.

signals.name: Findable
signals.description: Crawlable, indexed, accessible. Can AI bots reach and index the content?
signals.how_it_is_checked: AEONOS's llms.txt + robots.txt check fetches robots.txt and flags any Disallow rule targeting GPTBot, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot, or other AI crawlers, and checks whether /llms.txt exists.

signals.name: Understandable
signals.description: Clear language, logical structure. Can AI parse the content and understand what the page is about?
signals.how_it_is_checked: AEONOS's PAA/featured-snippet function counts question-format H2/H3 headings and checks for a real H2 hierarchy; the conversational-query function checks the opening 150 words for a clear 'what this is' statement.
score_blockers: marketing slogans as headings ('COLDBREW.ANYWHERE.' instead of 'What is freeze-dried cold brew?')
content is purely promotional with no informational value
signals.key_signal: Question-based headings (H2/H3) are a high-impact, well-established AEO/PAA signal. Rewrite service/product headings as the exact questions customers ask in ChatGPT and Google.

signals.name: Trustworthy
signals.description: Authority signals, schema markup. Does the site demonstrate credibility that AI systems can verify?
signals.how_it_is_checked: AEONOS's E-E-A-T assessment function checks for author attribution, an /about page, visible contact info, external authority links, privacy/terms, and a visible last-modified date, scoring 0-100.
score_blockers: no business contact info in text
implementation: Add Organization schema with name, url, logo, contactPoint, sameAs (social profiles)
Add LocalBusiness schema if physical location (include address, phone, opening hours)
Embed Google Reviews widget on homepage
Add visible ISO date stamps to all blog/service pages (confirms freshness)
Ensure business name, address, phone are in plain text sitewide — not embedded in images

signals.name: Extractable
signals.description: Sections that stand alone as citations. Can AI pull a paragraph and use it as a complete answer without needing more context?
signals.how_it_is_checked: AEONOS's schema extraction + gap analysis function parses JSON-LD/microdata/RDFa, validates required properties, and flags missing FAQPage/Article/Speakable schema with ready-to-paste JSON-LD templates generated from the page's own headings.
score_blockers: answers that don't include the question context
content that only makes sense with surrounding context
implementation: Add FAQPage schema markup — each answer must be a complete standalone response
Write answer-first paragraphs: lead with the answer, then elaborate
Each H2 section should work as a standalone citation — include enough context
40-60 words per answer is the sweet spot — enough detail, short enough to cite directly

signals.name: Reusable / Entity-Clear
signals.description: Format matches how AI constructs answers, and the entity itself (who/what this business is) is unambiguous. Is the content structured in the format AI tools actually use when synthesising responses?
signals.how_it_is_checked: AEONOS's entity disambiguation function checks name consistency across title/H1/schema, whether the ICP and outcome are stated in the opening copy, and whether an industry category is established; combined with the schema and PAA checks above for overall structure.
score_blockers: no step-by-step structure for process content
comparisons buried in prose rather than formatted as tables
implementation: Structure HowTo content as numbered steps with clear actions
Use bullet points for lists of features, benefits, requirements
Add HowTo schema for any process/tutorial content
Comparisons: use a table or a structured 'X vs Y' format
Definitions: one clear sentence, then elaboration

scoring.90-100: AI-ready — likely to be cited for branded and topical queries
scoring.70-89: Partially ready — will be cited for some queries, misses others
scoring.50-69: Significant gaps — AI tools will find the site but not cite it reliably
scoring.0-49: Not AI-ready — invisible to AI answer engines

geo: Add Google Reviews widget or embed to homepage
Add /llms.txt with business summary, services, FAQs
Add visible date stamps to all service/blog pages
Ensure business name, address, phone are in plain text on every page
aeo: Rewrite service/product headings as questions (e.g. 'What is osteopathy?' not 'Our Services')
Add answer-first paragraphs (40-60 words) under each question heading
Add FAQPage schema markup to FAQ section
Create a dedicated FAQ page targeting common customer questions
Add HowTo schema to treatment/process/tutorial pages
sxo: Ensure page loads under 3 seconds on mobile
Add BreadcrumbList schema to all inner pages
Add primary CTA on every service/product page
seo: Add LocalBusiness or Organization schema to homepage
Write unique meta descriptions for all pages (under 160 chars)
Add alt text to all images
Create location-specific or use-case-specific landing pages
technical: Add canonical tags to all pages
Submit XML sitemap to Google Search Console
Fix any crawl errors in Google Search Console
Enable HTTPS and check for mixed content warnings

content.priority: P1 — run this checklist before any other AEO work

content.title: llms.txt: Implementation Guide
content.summary: llms.txt is a structured file at your root domain that tells AI systems how to understand your business. Analogous to robots.txt but for AI crawlers.

format.structure: Markdown. Top section: business description. Then: products/services as headings. Then: key facts, pricing, target audience, what makes you different.
format.template:
# [Brand Name]

[1-2 sentence description of what you do and who you serve.]

## Products

### [Product Name]
[Price]. [What it does]. [Who it's for]. [Key benefit].

## Key Facts
- [Fact 1]
- [Fact 2]

## Target Audience
[Who your customer is — specific]

## What Makes Us Different
[Honest differentiator — not marketing fluff]

best_practices: Keep under 2000 words — AI context windows have limits, brevity gets read fully
Use factual, declarative language — not marketing copy
Update when products or pricing change
Include specific numbers: price, team size, customers served, founding date
Mention your founders by name — AI tools use named entities to build brand knowledge graphs
Include your key product category keywords naturally
Do NOT block llms.txt in robots.txt (common mistake)
content.robots_txt_note:
Add this to robots.txt to explicitly allow AI crawlers: 'User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /'

content.title: Competitor Analysis: SEO Gap Analysis Framework
content.summary: Find what competitors rank for that you don't, and find the underserved topics they've missed entirely.

steps.name: Identify real competitors
steps.detail: Search your top 3-5 target keywords in Google. Note who appears in the top 5. Also check: who appears in Perplexity and ChatGPT for those same queries. AI-visible competitors may differ from Google SERP competitors.

steps.name: Content gap analysis
steps.detail: For each competitor: what blog topics do they cover? What keywords do their pages target (visible in title tags)? What questions do they answer on their FAQ/pricing pages? List topics they've covered well, and topics they haven't touched.

steps.name: Link gap analysis
steps.detail: Use Ahrefs (paid) or free alternative: check who links to competitors that doesn't link to you. Those sites already link to content in your niche — they may link to you too.

steps.name: Differentiation angle
steps.detail: For new/small sites: don't try to outrank established domains on head terms. Find the underserved long-tail angle they haven't covered. A 2000-word guide on a specific use case beats competing on 'best [category]' with DR50+ sites.

steps.name: SERP type analysis
steps.detail: What content TYPE ranks for your target keywords? Blog posts, product pages, directories, YouTube, Reddit? If Reddit dominates, target Reddit. If it's all long-form guides, write a longer guide. Match the format that's working.

content.title: E-E-A-T Signals: What AI Tools Look for in Sources
content.summary: Google's Quality Rater Guidelines define E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness). AI tools use similar signals to decide which sources to cite.

implementation: Include case studies with real numbers
Write from personal experience — 'we found that', 'after running 50 campaigns'
Include photos, screenshots, real examples
Author bios with relevant credentials visible on page
Comprehensive, accurate content — no surface-level fluff
Cite sources with links to authoritative external references
Use correct industry terminology
Address nuance and edge cases, not just the main use case

authoritativeness.description: Recognition by others in the field
implementation: Backlinks from authoritative sites
Mentions in industry publications
Reviews and ratings on third-party platforms (G2, Capterra)
Speaking at conferences, podcast appearances
HTTPS (required)
Clear About page with team info
Privacy policy and terms of service
No misleading claims
Contact information visible
Reviews and testimonials (verified if possible)

content.ai_specific_note: AI tools weight authoritativeness and trustworthiness most heavily when choosing citation sources. A page with 3 authoritative backlinks and FAQ schema will be cited over a page with great content but no external validation.
content.priority: P2 — build on top of P1 schema and content work

content.title: Question-Based Headings: A High-Impact AEO/PAA Signal
content.summary: The single highest-impact AEO change on any page: rewrite H2/H3 headings as the exact questions customers type into ChatGPT and Google. AI systems match user queries to content by looking for literal question phrasing in headings.

the_signal.rule: Every H2 and H3 heading on a service, product, or blog page should be phrased as a question — the exact question a customer would type into ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google.
the_signal.why: AI search systems are built on question-answer matching. When a user asks 'What does an osteopath treat?', the AI looks for pages with that exact phrasing as a heading. A page with the heading 'Our Services' gets skipped. A page with 'What conditions does osteopathy treat?' gets cited.
the_signal.source: Rated '#1 AEO signal' by Pemba AI audit system's internal impact analysis

before_after_examples.after: What is freeze-dried cold brew coffee?
Who is [brand name] and what do we do?

implementation_steps: Audit every H2 and H3 on your key pages — list all headings
For each heading: ask 'what question would a customer type to land on this section?'
Rewrite the heading as that exact question
Write an answer-first paragraph immediately after (40-60 words, complete standalone answer)
Add FAQPage schema for the Q&A pairs you create
Repeat for all pages — prioritise: homepage, about, pricing, services/products, FAQ page

answer_format.rule: The paragraph immediately under each question heading must be a complete, standalone answer in 40-60 words. Lead with the answer — not background context.
answer_format.good_example: Osteopathy treats musculoskeletal conditions including back pain, neck pain, shoulder injuries, headaches, and sports injuries. It uses hands-on techniques to improve joint mobility, reduce muscle tension, and support the body's natural healing. Most patients see improvement within 2-3 sessions.
answer_format.bad_example: At Sherbourne House, our experienced team of practitioners takes a holistic approach to your health and wellbeing, drawing on years of clinical experience to provide tailored treatment plans that address your individual needs and goals.

content.title: Keyword Prioritization: The Sweet Spot Framework + Money-Pages-First Sequencing
content.summary: Score every keyword candidate against four attributes before committing content resources, then sequence content creation money-pages-first rather than informational-first.

sweet_spot_attributes.question: Where does it sit in the funnel, and is it relevant to what's actually offered?
Can the content satisfy what the searcher actually wants, including format (some SERPs demand video, not text)?
Is it realistic to rank given current site authority?

prioritization_sequence: 1. Build converting pages first — product/service/pricing pages targeting transactional and commercial keywords. This is what the business is actually built on. Common failure: writing lots of informational content before any money page exists, so there's nowhere for traffic to convert.

2. Pick ONE topical cluster connected to a money page and build the full funnel for it (money page → commercial comparison content → top-of-funnel educational content), all internally linked back down toward the money page.
3. Finish one cluster before starting the next — spreading thin across many clusters at once slows down topical authority and delays ranking results.
content.process: Ideation (Search Console query data, Google autosuggest, People Also Ask, subreddit language mining, LLM-assisted content-gap analysis) → Validation (check volume/difficulty/intent per idea before committing) → Clustering (group keywords Google treats as topically equivalent).
content.long_tail_note: Long-tail phrases carry lower individual volume but clearer intent and much lower competition — the right starting point for a newer/lower-authority site, building toward competitive head terms over time.
content.priority: P1 — must complete before creating any content

sources: SEO & AI SEO Course 2026 (tool-neutral transcript, cross-checked against independent market research)

content.title: Link Building: Three Tactics Ranked by Effort-to-Value (2026)
content.summary: Link building is the hardest, slowest part of SEO with no real shortcuts that don't risk penalty. Three practical tactics for a small operator, roughly in order of effort-to-value.

tactics.name: Be the source
tactics.detail: Original data, original analysis, or original resources that journalists/bloggers want to cite. Every business sits on some knowledge others would reference — most just never publish it.

tactics.name: Journalist query platforms
tactics.detail: Sign up for query platforms (successor tools to the old 'HARO' model), respond to journalist requests for expert quotes/sources with genuine expertise, get a citation/link when published. Low effort (~15 min/day), numbers-game conversion rate — the most accessible tactic for beginners.

tactics.name: Linkable assets
tactics.detail: Free tools, calculators, templates, or genuinely comprehensive guides that become reference material other sites want to link to instead of re-explaining the same thing. A narrow, cheap-to-build interactive tool tied to a real (even modest-volume) keyword can become a natural backlink magnet.

content.recommended_sequencing: For a smaller/newer site: build out 10-15 solid content pieces first, then start with journalist-query outreach (cheapest, fastest to start) before investing heavily in the other tactics — links compound over time once there's something worth linking to.

entries.query_pattern: how does AI search actually work what drives AI citation

content.title: AI Search Fundamentals: What Actually Drives AI Citation (2026)
content.summary: AI search engines are built on top of traditional search infrastructure, not a replacement for it. GEO is not a separate discipline from SEO — it's what happens when SEO fundamentals are done well and pointed at AI-readable structure.
content.core_thesis: ChatGPT's web search runs on Bing's index, Perplexity runs its own crawler but still leans on Bing underneath, and even sites with their own index are crawling the same pages that already rank in traditional search. Practical implication: if a site doesn't show up in Google/Bing, it's very unlikely to show up in AI assistant answers either.
content.measurement_blind_spot: Google Search Console cannot see traffic that originated from ChatGPT, Perplexity, or similar AI assistants — that referral data isn't exposed by the AI vendors. Actual AI-driven traffic can't be directly measured the way Google traffic can. Workaround: monitor whether a brand shows up when relevant questions are asked directly of AI assistants (run the query in an incognito/fresh session to avoid personalisation skewing results), tracked over time — not 'how many people came from there.'
what_drives_citation: Comprehensive, clearly-structured content that directly answers specific questions — LLMs pull cleanly from content organised this way.
Topical authority via full cluster coverage (definition + how-to + comparison + deep-dive on a subject), not single isolated pages.

Earning citations from other authoritative sources — AI models weight sources that other trusted sites already reference; backlinks function as a trust signal to AI systems too, not just to Google. AI assistants especially favour 'best-of' roundup articles.

Identifying and closing 'mention gaps' — which buyer-relevant queries competitors are already being AI-cited for that you aren't — and turning that gap list directly into an outreach/content priority list.
Checking AI visibility on a recurring basis, since AI-assistant recommendations shift meaningfully over time. This needs ongoing monitoring, not a one-off audit.
content.priority: P1 — foundational understanding required before any AI-search tactics

sources: SEO & AI SEO Course 2026 (tool-neutral transcript, cross-checked against independent market research)
